description: Build a Telegram-first text processing loop that ingests a message, normalizes interview questions, generates answers, writes Markdown locally, stores question-answer records for retrieval, and sends the generated answer text back to Telegram.

userStories.title: Bootstrap project and config loading
userStories.description: As the developer, I want a typed Python project skeleton with config loading so that the automation service has a maintainable foundation.
acceptanceCriteria: Project includes Python package structure for ingestion, workflows, storage, and dispatch modules
Configuration loads from environment variables with documented required keys
A CLI entry point or main module starts without continuous polling enabled
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Core scope. Existing base should be reused and tightened where needed.

userStories.title: Ingest Telegram text messages
userStories.description: As the user, I want to send a text message to a Telegram Bot so that interview content can enter the pipeline from my phone with minimal friction.
acceptanceCriteria: Telegram intake accepts plain text messages from the configured user or chat
Ingestion extracts message metadata needed to track source, time, and sender context
Unsupported or empty text messages fail clearly instead of crashing the bot flow
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Core scope. Focus this iteration on the text-first path only.

userStories.title: Persist raw Telegram bundles
userStories.description: As the system, I want to store raw Telegram text bundles locally so that later normalization and debugging have replayable inputs.
acceptanceCriteria: Each ingested Telegram text message is stored as a deterministic raw artifact bundle
Raw bundles include enough metadata to trace back to the original Telegram message
Stored raw bundles can be reloaded by downstream workflows
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Core scope. Reuse the SourceBundle abstraction.

userStories.title: Normalize text bundles into questions
userStories.description: As the user, I want Telegram text bundles transformed into structured interview questions so that answer generation is focused and reusable.
acceptanceCriteria: LangGraph workflow accepts a text-first SourceBundle input and outputs a typed normalized JSON document
Normalization filters obvious non-interview noise from the source content
Normalization stops clearly when the input text is too sparse to produce meaningful questions
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Core scope. Text-first quality matters more than broad source coverage.

userStories.title: Generate retrieval-aware answers
userStories.description: As the user, I want both detailed and concise answers for normalized interview questions, using similar prior records when available, so that I can study deeply or review quickly.
acceptanceCriteria: Generation step can retrieve similar prior records before generating answers when history exists
Generation step consumes normalized question data and retrieved context to produce a detailed answer set
Generation step produces a concise review version suitable for mobile reading
Generated outputs are typed and persisted independently from raw source content
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Core scope. Retrieval should be part of the path, but the first bundle may have little or no historical context yet.

userStories.title: Persist local JSON and Markdown artifacts
userStories.description: As the user, I want processed outputs saved locally as JSON and Markdown so that I can inspect and review them outside Telegram.
acceptanceCriteria: Service writes deterministic per-bundle JSON artifacts for raw, normalized, and generated outputs
Service writes a Markdown answer artifact suitable for quick reading and archival review
Artifact generation does not depend on Telegram delivery succeeding
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Core scope. Markdown is the primary human-readable archive.

userStories.title: Store question-answer records in vector storage
userStories.description: As the user, I want both questions and generated answers stored for retrieval and later organization so that study materials accumulate over time.
acceptanceCriteria: Vector storage keeps normalized question records early enough for later bundles to retrieve them before generation
Vector storage keeps full question-answer records after generation rather than only question embeddings
Stored records include enough metadata to trace back to bundle id and local artifact paths
Insertion skips malformed or empty records without crashing the workflow
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Core scope. Retrieval should support later archival and organization, not just immediate grounding.

userStories.title: Reply to Telegram with generated answer text
userStories.description: As the user, I want the generated answer text sent back to Telegram so that I can review results on mobile immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: Telegram dispatcher sends a readable text reply based on the generated answer artifacts
Reply formatting stays within Telegram text constraints or degrades clearly when too long
Dispatcher records success or failure status for the outbound message
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Core scope. Telegram reply should reuse the generated answer artifacts instead of regenerating content inline.

userStories.title: Add one-shot automatic orchestration
userStories.description: As the user, I want a newly ingested Telegram text message to automatically continue through normalization, answer generation, local archival, vector insertion, and Telegram reply so that the flow works end to end without manual command chaining.
acceptanceCriteria: A single command or bot action can process a new Telegram text bundle from ingestion to final outputs
The orchestration stops clearly at the failing stage if one step fails
Successful steps are not silently skipped and final outputs are verifiable on disk
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Core scope. This is the core usability gap between working components and a true end-to-end flow.

userStories.title: Add OCR or multimodal media extraction
userStories.description: As the user, I want screenshot-heavy bundles to be readable so that image-first interview posts can also enter the same pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: Downloaded Telegram assets can be converted into text with OCR or multimodal models
Media-derived text can be merged into the same SourceBundle-driven normalization path
Media extraction failures are surfaced clearly without corrupting the original raw bundle
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Optional scope. Important for real usage, but not required for the first text-first end-to-end path.

userStories.title: Add Telegram message grouping
userStories.description: As the user, I want related Telegram messages sent close together to be grouped into one logical bundle so that links and follow-up text are processed together.
acceptanceCriteria: Related Telegram messages from the same chat can be merged into one processing bundle under clear rules
Message grouping improves multi-part text inputs without corrupting unrelated messages
Grouped bundles remain replayable and traceable to the original message ids
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Optional scope. This is a usability improvement after the first text-only core loop works.

userStories.title: Add Feishu source adapter
userStories.description: As the user, I want Feishu messages to enter the same pipeline so that another collaboration tool can reuse the SourceBundle-based workflow.
acceptanceCriteria: Feishu inbound events can be mapped into the shared SourceBundle schema
Feishu-derived bundles can reuse existing normalization, indexing, generation, archival, and reply flows without source-specific redesign
Adapter-specific metadata is preserved for debugging
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Optional scope. Validates that SourceBundle truly supports multi-source expansion.
